actions.label: Provide food rations for guards and their families
Have FWB representatives directly manage disbursement at distribution points
Allow FWB staff unescorted, unrestricted movement in the camp
Allow guards to take part in distribution alongside FWB staff
Provide ongoing, scheduled food aid deliveries to the camp
Fund guard pay and generator needs from government/militia sources instead of FWB
Permit FWB nutritional assessments under escort and security arrangements
Accept food being used as payment for guards and workers
Allow FWB representatives to manage or oversee food disbursement directly
Provide guard security at distribution points and perimeter, running distribution block by block
Assign guards and militia to organize distribution jointly with FWB

goals.label: Accurate needs information and documentation for donors
Food aid is diverted, skimmed or confiscated by guards or militia
Food aid reaches the camp on an ongoing, sustainable basis
Food functions as currency and payment in the camp
Camp authorities and militia control food distribution
Camp generators keep running with fuel and parts
Commander's authority and standing are preserved
FWB controls and oversees food distribution
FWB remains neutral and does not support armed actors
FWB staff have access and freedom of movement in the camp
Food is distributed fairly and equally to all refugees
Guards and their families are fed and paid, keeping them loyal
Host town welfare and local economy are protected
Nutritional assessments are intrusive, slow or resource-heavy and control of camp information
Order is maintained in the camp without riots or violence
Outsiders move freely and unescorted in the camp
Refugees receive adequate food and nutrition
Refugees remain contained in the camp and away from the capital
Safety of FWB staff and local assistants
Commander keeps the trust and backing of the Senior Militia Leader
FWB's reputation and visibility of its work
Government and militia funding for camp operations
Hostile actors exploit outside access to carry out attacks

redLines.label: Accept FWB-chosen local assistants in distribution, prioritizing local hires
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Hire FWB-chosen local assistants from the host community
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
